title: Respiratory microbiome and clinical data analysis for the prediction of acute exacerbations in COPD - Longitudinal study
summary: Acute worsening of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a major factor in morbidity, loss of quality of life and necessity for medical consultation for patients. Frequency and course of these worsening situations vary from patient too patient. Right now, methods to estimate the risk for a patient is based on anamnestic questions, clinical signs and sociodemographic parameters. A large proportion a worsening is associated with acute airway infections. In the REDALERT study, the aim is to investigate whether information about the composition of bacteria in the lung can improve these predictions and ultimately lead to an earlier recognition of these situations.
conditions: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute lower respiratory infection
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation, unspecified

interventions.name:
Duration of the study will be one year for each participant. Participants will start the study with a baseline visit in a clinical stable condition. This will consist of a clinical examination, throat swab, sputum and blood sampling and lung function tests as well as symptom questionnaires.
Partici

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Written informed consent
2. Physician-confirmed diagnosis of COPD (spirometry) (FEV1 ≤ 80% predicted)
3. Smoking history: Min. 10 packyears
Exclusion criteria:
1.Inability to understand the nature, scope, and possible consequences of the study
2. Life expectancy of less than 12 months
3. Newly diagnosed active pulmonary tuberculosis within the last 12 months
4. Unstable cardiopulmonary or metabolic co-morbidities
5. Macrolide maintenance treatment
